name: Houston (US-TX)
role: Largest US crude export and petrochemical complex
roleNotes: The 52-mile Houston Ship Channel hosts Enterprise's LPG and ethane export docks at Morgan's Point, the Kinder Morgan and ONEOK refined-product hubs at Pasadena and Galena Park, the ExxonMobil Baytown and Pemex Deer Park refineries and the US Gulf Coast's main residual-fuel and bunkering market, and is one of the two largest US crude export points.

wikipedia.title: Port of Houston
wikipedia.extract: The Port of Houston is one of the world's largest ports and serves the metropolitan area of Houston, Texas. The port is a 50-mile-long (80 km) complex of diversified public and private facilities located a few hours' sailing time from the Gulf of Mexico. Located in the fourth-largest city in the United States, it is the busiest port in the U.S. in terms of foreign tonnage and the busiest in the U.S. in terms of overall tonnage. Though originally the port's terminals were primarily within the Houston city limits, the port has expanded to such a degree that today it has facilities in multiple communities in the surrounding area. In particular the port's busiest terminal, the Barbours Cut Terminal, is located in Morgan's Point.
